description: Short original summaries of selected public MedlinePlus topics, packaged for offline retrieval. Not comprehensive, not a clinical guideline. External URLs are bibliographic only.

entries.title: Blood cholesterol and LDL
entries.summary: Cholesterol and triglycerides are measured in blood to help assess cardiovascular risk. LDL goals depend on individual risk and medical history; no single cutoff fits everyone. Diet patterns emphasizing vegetables, whole grains, soluble fiber, legumes and unsaturated fats can help. Limit saturated and trans fats. A clinician assesses total risk, other conditions, and whether treatment is needed.
entries.source_title: Cholesterol Levels: What You Need to Know — MedlinePlus

entries.title: Vitamin D deficiency
entries.summary: Vitamin D helps with calcium absorption and bone health. Deficiency may be associated with bone weakness; severe deficiency can cause rickets in children or osteomalacia in adults. Fortified foods, fatty fish and other dietary sources can contribute, but personal needs and test interpretation should be discussed with a clinician. Do not recommend supplement doses based on one result.

entries.title: Iron deficiency and anemia
entries.summary: Iron deficiency can lead to anemia and symptoms such as fatigue, weakness, dizziness or breathlessness. Blood counts, ferritin and other tests help investigate causes, which may include dietary intake or blood loss. Iron-rich foods include lentils, beans, meat and leafy greens; vitamin C can support absorption from plant foods. Supplements and causes of bleeding need professional review.
entries.source_title: Iron deficiency anemia — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

entries.title: Vitamin B12 deficiency
entries.summary: Vitamin B12 is needed for healthy red blood cells and nervous-system function. Deficiency may cause tiredness, anemia, numbness or tingling and can have several dietary or absorption-related causes. Animal-derived foods and fortified foods may supply B12. Investigation and appropriate treatment should be supervised by a clinician, particularly with neurologic symptoms.

entries.title: Diabetes and HbA1c
entries.summary: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over about three months and helps assess diabetes or prediabetes. Certain blood disorders can affect the test's accuracy. Diagnosis and treatment require appropriate clinical assessment and sometimes repeat testing. Dietary choices often focus on balanced meals, high-fiber foods, and limiting sugary drinks; individual plans vary.

entries.title: Thyroid function and TSH
entries.summary: TSH is one test used in assessing thyroid function. An underactive or overactive thyroid can cause symptoms involving energy, weight, bowel habits, temperature tolerance and heart rate. Interpretation depends on reference ranges, age, symptoms, medication and often other thyroid tests. Food or supplements are not substitutes for medical evaluation.

entries.title: High blood pressure and DASH eating pattern
entries.summary: Persistently high blood pressure increases cardiovascular risk and may have no symptoms. Accurate repeated readings and clinician assessment matter. The DASH eating pattern emphasizes vegetables, fruits, whole grains and less sodium. Potassium-containing foods or salt substitutes are not universally suitable, especially with kidney disease or certain medicines.
entries.source_title: High blood pressure and diet — MedlinePlus

entries.title: Kidney function and eGFR
entries.summary: eGFR estimates kidney filtration from blood-based measures and personal factors; its meaning depends on context and sometimes repeated measurements and urine tests. Kidney conditions can affect appropriate dietary advice for salt, potassium, protein and fluids. Do not recommend a universal kidney diet or interpret a single number as a diagnosis.
entries.source_title: Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) and GFR Tests — MedlinePlus
